summary: A notice that the socket supporting the TIP News facility at BBN-TENEX moved to socket 367 octal. TIP users were not affected, but because some Telnet programs had a news command, the old socket would remain until April 15, 1973 to give implementers time to switch.

eli5.summary: A shop moved to a new door number and kept the old door open for a while so people had time to learn the new one.

subtitle: Notice of socket change for the TIP News facility at BBN-TENEX

tldr.problem: The TIP News facility at BBN-TENEX needed to move from its existing socket to a new socket to better organize network services.
tldr.mechanism: The socket for the TIP News facility was changed from its old address to socket 367 octal. TIP users were unaffected since the TIP program had already been updated. User Telnet programs with a hardcoded news command were given until April 15, 1973 to update to the new socket address.
tldr.outcome: The migration proceeded with a grace period for software to be updated, minimizing disruption while allowing the infrastructure change.

today: RFC 470 is a brief administrative notice from the early ARPANET. The socket addressing scheme it references was replaced by IP addresses and port numbers in modern networks. The TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) was an early network access device that was eventually superseded by personal computers and modern networking.

sections.title: Socket Migration for News Service
sections.content: Bob Thomas of BBN-TENEX announced that the socket supporting the TIP News facility had been changed to socket 367 octal at BBN-TENEX. In the ARPANET architecture of the time, sockets were the endpoints for network communication, roughly analogous to ports in modern networks. This change reorganized the network addressing scheme for the news service, which provided network updates and information to TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) users.
sections.eli5: The service that sends news to the network moved to a new address number to make things better organized.

sections.title: Backwards Compatibility
sections.content: TIP users who accessed the news facility through the TIP program directly were unaffected by the change, since the TIP program had already been updated to connect to the new socket. However, because some network implementers had written Telnet programs with hardcoded news commands that pointed to the old socket, the old socket was maintained until April 15, 1973. This grace period gave software implementers sufficient time to update their user Telnet programs to use the new socket address without breaking existing deployments.
sections.eli5: Regular TIP users didn't notice anything, but people who built their own programs had a few weeks to fix them.

sections.title: Transition Timeline
sections.content: The change was announced on March 13, 1973, and the old socket would remain active until April 15, 1973. This three-month window was designed to be sufficient for network implementers to update their Telnet news client code. The grace period reflected the communication and development constraints of the era, when software updates required manual intervention and coordination across the distributed ARPANET.
sections.eli5: Everyone had a couple of months to make their programs talk to the new address before the old one stopped working.
